verified.notes: GGUF filenames and byte sizes were checked with HTTP HEAD against Hugging Face (x-linked-size). llama-server flags were checked against the llama.cpp server README at tag b12110 (the binary release pointed at by the v0.9.0 nightly-tag.txt). Nothing in this file was executed on an RTX 4070. The setup script resolves the latest llama.cpp release instead of pinning b12110.

quality.description: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, about 3B parameters active. Primary overnight model. Thinking is on, and each agent turn is allowed a large completion budget so the reply is not empty.

expected.vram: Roughly 5 to 7.5 GiB at 40K context with n-cpu-moe 34. A published 12 GB / 16 GB sizing note for this same Unsloth UD-Q4_K_M file puts expert tensors near 0.45 GiB per layer across 40 layers, with about 1.9 GiB of non-expert weights on GPU after the embedding stays on CPU, and about 0.8 GiB of FP16 KV at 40K because only 10 layers are full attention. The witcheer 8GB bench (RTX 4060 Ti, May 2026) used n-cpu-moe 30 and recorded 7.2 GB, which is tight once Windows is using the laptop GPU.
expected.ram: The 20.6 GiB file is mmap'd. With most experts on CPU, plan on about 22 GiB resident plus the OS. 32 GB is enough if other large apps are closed and a page file exists. Do not pass --mlock.
expected.speed: The same bench reported about 35 tok/s decode at n-cpu-moe 30 on a desktop 4060 Ti, and thinking mode made wall-clock time much worse because the model spends tokens on reasoning. A Legion 4070 with n-cpu-moe 34 should land in a similar band, not in the hundreds of tok/s. This was not measured on a 4070 laptop.

quality.notes: Shipped n-cpu-moe is 34, not the bench's 30, so a laptop display and CUDA context have room under 8 GB. Run scripts/tune-n-cpu-moe.ps1 -Profile quality once; it writes runtime/overrides.json. --fit is off so llama.cpp cannot silently shrink the 40K context. --n-predict -1 lets the request max_tokens be the cap; a small server-side -n is what makes thinking models return an empty content field. Repeat penalty stays at 1. Batch 512 keeps the CUDA compute buffer smaller than the 2048 the official gpt-oss guide uses on roomier cards.

day.description: gpt-oss-20b native MXFP4. The reliable daytime agent model from the May 2026 8GB VRAM bench. All experts stay on CPU at the shipped setting.

expected.vram: The witcheer bench recorded 1.8 GB VRAM with n-cpu-moe 30, -c 32768, -n 8192, --jinja on an RTX 4060 Ti 8GB. n-cpu-moe 30 is above this model's 24 layers, so every expert block is on CPU and the GPU holds attention plus KV. That is why it fit with headroom when larger dense models did not.
expected.ram: About 12 GiB for weights, comfortable next to Windows on 32 GB.
expected.speed: Decode is limited by system-RAM bandwidth, not by the 4070's shader rate. Expect tens of tokens per second. The bench completed 10/10 agent tasks with Pi's read/write/edit/bash tools at these settings. Not measured on a 4070 laptop.

day.notes: Use the ggml-org MXFP4 file. gpt-oss is already 4-bit; a second quantization to Q4_K_M throws away the native format. The harmony chat template is inside the GGUF and needs --jinja, which this profile passes explicitly even though llama-server 0.9 defaults jinja on. reasoning_effort medium is the template default. Set reasoning_effort to high in runtime/overrides.json for a harder daytime task. OpenAI's sampling recommendation for gpt-oss is temperature 1.0. Agent max_tokens is 8192 to match the bench, with one automatic retry up to 16384 when a turn comes back empty.

max.description: Dense Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M with FFN weights on CPU. Slow on purpose. Not downloaded unless you ask for it.

expected.vram: All 64 dense FFN blocks start on CPU (--n-cpu-ffn 64) and attention stays on the GPU (--n-gpu-layers all). That is the dense equivalent of expert offload. Context is 16K because this model has 16 full-attention layers and a long context will crowd an 8 GB card. The tuner can lower n-cpu-ffn if nvidia-smi shows room.
expected.ram: About 18 GiB of weights mapped into RAM, plus KV and the OS. Tight on 32 GB. Close other applications. The official ggml-org repo does not publish a Q3_K_M of this file; if the machine swaps, the practical next step is a smaller context, not a different architecture.
expected.speed: Every token reads the dense FFN from system RAM. Expect this to be several times slower than the MoE profiles. It is an overnight experiment, not a daytime driver.

max.notes: Qwen3.8-27B's template defaults reasoning effort to xhigh. This profile asks for high so a turn can finish inside the token budget; put xhigh in overrides if you want the template default and can afford the extra tokens. There is no --n-cpu-moe on a dense model. Do not point the agent at a 7B-9B model: in the same 8GB bench those models broke multi-step tool calls even when single-file generation looked fine.
